title: Secure GET /users listing endpoint
summary: Implemented and hardened a read-only Flask GET /users endpoint that returns id, username, and email from SQLite using a static parameterized query, safe error handling, and deterministic ordering.

threats_mitigated.description: Untrusted input concatenated into SELECT statements could expose or mutate the users table.
threats_mitigated.mitigation_applied: Use a static SQL statement with no user-controlled fragments; only id, username, email are selected.

threats_mitigated.description: SQLite exceptions returned to clients could leak schema or query details.
threats_mitigated.mitigation_applied: Catch sqlite3.Error and return a generic JSON error with HTTP 500; no stack traces or SQL text in the response.

threats_mitigated.description: Returning full user rows could leak sensitive columns if added later.
threats_mitigated.mitigation_applied: Explicit column projection (id, username, email) in the query and JSON response.

threats_mitigated.description: A public list endpoint allows anyone to enumerate all users.
threats_mitigated.mitigation_applied: Accepted as intentional for this simple demo endpoint; documented residual risk. Production would require authentication and authorization.

best_practices_achieved: Static parameterized SQL with explicit column allowlist
try/finally ensures database connections are closed
Generic error responses without internal details

secure_code_snippets.explanation: Read-only list endpoint with static query, field projection, safe error handling, and guaranteed connection cleanup.

guardrails_applied.title: Do not build queries or commands with string concatenation
guardrails_applied.instruction: Don't concatenate untrusted input into SQL/NoSQL/LDAP/OS command templates. Use parameterized APIs and safe query builders.
guardrails_applied.notes: GET /users uses a static SELECT with no interpolated user input.

guardrails_applied.title: Eliminate vulnerability classes structurally, not by case-by-case patching
guardrails_applied.instruction: For each class CISA highlights (SQLi, XSS, command injection, path traversal, memory-safety bugs), pick a structural mitigation rather than per-callsite review: parameterized queries / ORM-only DB access; auto-escaping templates (no raw HTML interpolation); a single command-runner that refuses string concatenation; a path-join helper that rejects '..'; memory-safe languages for new code. Lint/CI rules should fail builds that bypass these.
guardrails_applied.notes: Structural SQLi mitigation via static query builder pattern on this route.

guardrails_applied.title: Do not return verbose internal errors to users
guardrails_applied.instruction: Don't expose stack traces, SQL errors, framework debug pages, or internal identifiers in responses. Return generic errors with correlation IDs.
guardrails_applied.notes: sqlite3.Error handler returns generic message without SQL details.

guardrails_applied.title: Do not expose secrets in source, logs, or error messages
guardrails_applied.instruction: Don't hardcode credentials, include secrets in stack traces, or log tokens/keys/session IDs; load secrets from managed secret stores.
guardrails_applied.notes: Error path does not log or return exception details.

guardrails_applied.title: Validate and canonicalize all untrusted input server-side
guardrails_applied.instruction: Use allowlists, strict schemas, and length/type/range checks for all request data, file metadata, headers, and external API payloads.
guardrails_applied.notes: Endpoint accepts no request parameters; N/A for input validation on this route.

guardrails_applied.title: Enforce least-privilege and deny-by-default authorization
guardrails_applied.instruction: Apply server-side authorization checks on every protected action and object reference; default to deny when policy evaluation is unavailable.
guardrails_applied.notes: Intentionally public read-only demo endpoint; production would gate behind authz policy.
